intro: Opposite Dalyan, on the border between Caria and Lycia, lies a harbour city watched over by tombs cut into the cliffs. You have arrived at the Ancient City of Kaunos, in Muğla province. Its story begins in the 10th century BC, and it is famed for its impressive rock-cut tombs.
history: Kaunos was founded in the 10th century BC and grew into an important trading city with two harbours. The Persians, Rhodes and Rome ruled it in turn. But the Dalyan river silted up, filling its harbours and cutting it off from the sea. The final blow was a malaria epidemic, which led to its abandonment in the 15th century AD.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Theatre, the Rock-cut Tombs, the Agora, the Roman Baths and the Byzantine Church.
facts: Did you know? Around 150 rock-cut tombs are carved into the cliff face. The temple-fronted ones date to the 4th century BC and show Lycian influence; cut as temple façades, they face you head-on as the boat passes down the Dalyan river. The harbour itself silted into a lake, leaving a maritime city stranded behind the reed beds. And the malaria left its mark on the people: ancient writers describe the Caunians as sallow, and Strabo remarks on their greenish complexion.
outro: This brings our journey through the Ancient City of Kaunos to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
